Some said that whether the DSRB can offer cheaper financing than highly rated national governments was a stumbling block for some potential members. The amount of capital countries would need to commit while public finances are strained, the bank's governance, and overlaps with existing initiatives were also cited as factors. Canada says it is talking with [USN:L6N4390PM TEXT:"many countries"] ahead of a charter signing that its lead negotiator for the DSRB, Isabelle Hudon, said on the sidelines of July's Farnborough Airshow was planned for the autumn. "We are proceeding at pace, developing Articles of Agreement and working with allies and partners alike to form a group of founding nations," said John Fragos, press secretary for Canada's finance minister. REARMAMENT PUSH Speaking at Farnborough on a panel dedicated to defence investment, DSRB founder Rob Murray said the lender would help countries rearm to counter mounting security threats. "We need 10 of them, frankly," the former British Army officer and NATO innovation chief said. European countries are increasing defence spending after the Trump administration demanded they [USN:L1N3XC05V TEXT:"take on more"] of NATO's burden, although [USN:L8N4391TG TEXT:"few are close"] to meeting the alliance's latest targets. Carney earlier this year called for an alliance of [USN:L6N3YM16S TEXT:""middle powers""] to respond to what he sees as the fracturing of the U.S.-led world order. The DSRB will "ensure that Canada and our Allies have the capacity to meet the challenges of a more dangerous and divided world together", he said in July. Perraudin said the DSRB could use financial leverage separate from the balance sheets of already indebted nations to boost defence investment. To become a significant player, however, it would need additional sovereign backing beyond current commitments, he said. While big European economies can already borrow cheaply, membership would ensure their domestic contractors can access the DSRB funding, said Linus Terhorst of the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) think tank. COMPETING INITIATIVES Five of the people with knowledge of the talks about DSRB membership cited potential overlap with other financing efforts, including the EU's SAFE programme and Britain's proposed Multilateral Defence Mechanism. The European Union launched its €150 billion [USN:L5N3RZ0GJ TEXT:"SAFE"] (Security Action for Europe) defence financing programme in 2025, while Britain is developing a [USN:L1N4380L2 TEXT:"Multilateral Defence Mechanism"] (MDM) with the Netherlands, Finland and Poland focused on joint procurement. One official also cited concerns about the upfront capital required from governments, as well as uncertainty over how projects would be selected. Larger countries have been asked to put forward around €1 billion, two people with knowledge of the plans said. In emailed comments to Reuters, Murray said this could be paid over three years and would in time return profits through dividends, while the DSRB would provide a more permanent institution for financing defence than SAFE and could work with any procurement method. "If we do this properly, higher defence expenditure can generate technology, factories, skilled jobs, stronger supply chains and economic growth while simultaneously strengthening deterrence," Murray said. WOOING BRITAIN Canada hopes Britain could reconsider under new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, whose defence minister Wes Streeting described the DSRB at Farnborough as a "really interesting and innovative mechanism". He also said he did not see the proposed defence bank and MDM as being in competition. Britain previously [USN:L1N3UR0C7 TEXT:"declined to join"], citing concerns over value for money. According to his Downing Street office, Burnham discussed the DSRB alongside the MDM scheme with Carney in July and with Luxembourg Prime Minister [USN:L8N44L0BK TEXT:"Luc Frieden"] during an August visit to Kyiv. "The UK joining would create pressure from German industry on the German government to join," said RUSI's Terhorst. A German finance ministry spokesperson said its position on the DSRB had not changed since July, when it told Reuters it had taken part in DSRB talks as an observer and was reviewing the outcome. Japan's foreign ministry told Reuters no decision had been made about participating. British and German industry groups have lobbied their countries to join. Andrew Kinniburgh of Make UK Defence said companies risked being excluded from projects financed through the bank if Britain stayed out. CHASING A TRIPLE-A RATING About a dozen [USN:L6N3YY0XA TEXT:"banks"] including JPMorgan (JPM.N) and Deutsche Bank (DBKGn.DE) have provided some $10 million in funding or services in kind to help establish the DSRB, according to a person with knowledge of the matter. The lenders, which could earn millions in fees arranging DSRB-funded projects, also backed an advertisement in the Financial Times newspaper saying the project had "the hallmarks of a future AAA-rated multilateral financial institution". JPMorgan and Deutsche Bank declined to comment. Canada's Hudon said at Farnborough that she was confident the DSRB could get a triple-A rating. Murray said a multilateral bank's rating depends on many factors and often exceeds the average rating of members. Ottawa is prepared to launch the bank with the current group of supporters, one person involved in the project said, with other countries free to join later. That could help cement the rating it wants. "The creditworthiness of multilateral institutions is principally driven by the support of their core shareholders," said Elisabeth Rudman, head of financial institution ratings at Morningstar DBRS. ($1 = 0.8590 euros)

item.title: Chelsea sign goalkeeper Martinez from Villa on three-year deal
item.description: Chelsea have signed goalkeeper Emiliano "Dibu" Martinez from Aston Villa on a three-year deal, the West London club said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chelsea have signed goalkeeper Emiliano "Dibu" Martinez from Aston Villa on a three-year deal, the West London club said on Sunday. Financial details were not disclosed, but British media reported that Chelsea paid around £7.5 million ($10.15 million) to sign the 33-year-old. "I want to be successful here," Martinez said in a statement. "I'm someone who wants to win at everything I do and I want to bring that here to this football club because it's a football club that wins titles, so I think it's a good match." Martinez's exit comes after Villa signed Japan international Zion Suzuki from Parma earlier this month, paving the way for the Argentine's exit after six years at Villa Park. Martinez made 256 appearances for Villa after joining from Arsenal in 2020 and established himself as one of the Premier League's leading goalkeepers. He played a key role last season as Unai Emery's side finished fourth to qualify for the Champions League and won the Europa League. At Chelsea, Martinez is set to challenge Robert Sanchez for the starting role. Sanchez has been Chelsea's first-choice goalkeeper since arriving from Brighton & Hove Albion in 2023, but questions over his place resurfaced [USN:L1N44L0X2 TEXT:"after mistakes in Chelsea's 3-2"] opening-day victory over Fulham. Martinez has also been central to Argentina's success on the international stage, helping them win the 2022 FIFA World Cup and finish runners-up in 2026. The first-choice goalkeeper also won Copa America titles in 2021 and 2024. His departure is the latest significant exit for Villa during a busy transfer window. Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea for a British record fee, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Jadon Sancho, Douglas Luiz and Lucas Digne have also left the club. ($1 = 0.7390 pounds)

item.title: U.S. Open has record prize money but pushes back on revenue-share model
item.description: The United States Tennis Association has answered player demands for greater compensation with record-breaking prize money at the U.S. Open that starts on Sunday in Flushing, N.Y.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States Tennis Association has answered player demands for greater compensation with record-breaking prize money at the U.S. Open that starts on Sunday in Flushing, N.Y. The creation of a new player support program and the Grand Slam Player Advisory Council also has been received positively. One issue at the heart of any upcoming discussions, however -- a larger revenue share from Grand Slam tournaments -- appears to be a non-starter for the USTA. Craig Tiley, who officially became USTA CEO last month, said at a press conference on Saturday that the grand slam tournament does not determine prize money based on revenue. "We don't use that number as a form of calculating how we compensate, because it can be fairly arbitrary from one event to another," Tiley said, per Front Office Sports. "I believe the tours use profit, so we look at it very differently. We say, what's a fair share that the players need to be compensated on, and what can we do, because even outside of just the compensation package, what other things can we do to help support the players, not just during the event but also year-round." The U.S. Open has boosted the prize pool by 20%, including a Grand Slam-record $5.5 million to this year's singles champions. The overall compensation is a record $108 million, up from $90 million last year and a whopping 44% jump from $75 million in 2024. Every player who makes the 128-player main singles draw will earn at least $140,000, the largest in tennis history. Quarterfinalists will earn $780,000 and semifinalists will get $1.45 million, with $2.8 million going to the runners-up. Last year's champions -- Spain's Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka of Belarus -- each earned a winner's check of $5 million. By comparison, the prize pools for the other 2026 Grand Slam tournaments were: Wimbledon (about $87.5 million), French Open (about $71.7 million) and the Australian Open (about $79.3 million). According to Front Office Sports, Grand Slam tournaments don't have a fixed share of revenue in place, instead generally paying out about 15% of revenue to players. The players, however, are targeting a 22% share by 2030. Top players have said that the goal of higher Grand Slam purses is to help lower-ranked players who are trying to start or sustain their careers. Also among the players' demands are improved retirement benefits and a better focus on player welfare during the two-week Grand Slams. "You will see the U.S. Open continue to be a very player-friendly event," Tiley said Saturday, per Front Office Sports. "I think our desire to increase the amount that we put on the table was driven really within the organization, the sense that we need to give the players a fair share." Jessica Pegula, the No. 3 women's singles player in the world, told Front Office Sports on Friday that revenue sharing will be a key topic for the Grand Slam Advisory Council. "That's something we're still pushing for, and so I think hopefully with this council, that we'll be able to continue those discussions because I know from our side, we still do believe that a revenue share is the best way, and now we'll just have much more open communication," said Pegula, a member of the WTA Players' Council. She lauded the USTA for creating the new council but said Friday that more information is needed. Tiley said on Saturday that about 10 players have expressed interest in joining the council. "We think, again, the voice of the players, we believe, is important," Tiley said, per Front Office Sports. "Many of us have been spending a lot of time and energy individually talking to the players. Not just the last week -- it's been going on for years. The Slams having a close player relationship is critical to the success of the Slams and the success of the relationship that we have with the fans, as well." --Field Level Media

item.title: Niger says it regains control of airbase after soldiers mutiny
item.description: Niger said it had regained control of a key military airbase in the capital Niamey after an attack by mutinous soldiers on Saturday, in the latest challenge to military ruler Abdourahamane Tiani as his government struggles to contain a jihadist insurgency.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Niger said it had regained control of a key military airbase in the capital Niamey after an [USN:L1N44Q00F TEXT:"attack"] by mutinous soldiers on Saturday, in the latest challenge to military ruler Abdourahamane Tiani as his government struggles to contain a jihadist insurgency. The attack highlighted tensions within Niger's armed forces, which have suffered repeated battlefield losses while fighting West Africa's al Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates. Explosions and gunfire rang out across Niamey early on Saturday, including at the military airbase and around the presidency. Located in the same complex as Niamey's civilian airport, the airbase is home to military aircraft and drones as well as a counter-terrorism unit of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) which includes Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso. Russian and Italian forces are also stationed there. Africa Corps, a Kremlin-controlled paramilitary force, received a request for assistance in neutralising the mutineers in Niamey, Viktor Voropaev, the Russian ambassador to Niger, said on Saturday in an interview with TASS news agency. Prior to Saturday's attack, the airbase had already been targeted twice this year - in January by the regional Islamic State affiliate and in June by the regional al Qaeda affiliate. Niger state media said late Saturday that the attack involved "hundreds of disaffected soldiers" and that fighting lasted for several hours as forces loyal to military leader Tiani tried to regain control. It aired footage purporting to show surrendering mutineers. Reuters has not independently confirmed the state media report. The Presidential Guard rallied to Tiani's defence, three security sources said. Tiani had not made any public appearances as of Sunday morning. Niger, a West African nation rich in uranium, oil and gold resources, has been ruled by military officers since a July 2023 coup that ousted President Mohamed Bazoum. SAHEL LEADERS STRUGGLE AGAINST JIHADISTS Tiani, like his counterparts in Burkina Faso and Mali, has failed to make progress against jihadists. The Islamic State affiliate has staged multiple deadly assaults on the military in southwest Niger, including one earlier this month that killed 18 soldiers. The mutineers' operation involved soldiers based in Niamey as well as soldiers from the localities of Ouallam, Tera and Dosso, where the army has sustained heavy casualties. Analysts and security sources say frustration with the government is mounting within frontline units, creating another vulnerability for Tiani beyond the insurgents themselves. Since seizing power, Tiani's government has shifted away from Western partners, deepened ties with Russia and broken with the regional ECOWAS bloc. The unrest comes as authorities tighten control over the uranium sector, having [USN:L8N3XA11V TEXT:"seized assets"] from France's Orano. Niger had been a key supplier of nuclear fuel to Europe, accounting for about 15% of Orano's uranium supply at full capacity.

item.title: Team Liquid wins again, could wrap up LCS Summer Split top seed
item.description: The way Team Liquid is playing, the No. 1 seed in the League Championship Series Summer Split playoffs may be decided before the final week of the regular season even begins.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The way Team Liquid is playing, the No. 1 seed in the League Championship Series Summer Split playoffs may be decided before the final week of the regular season even begins. Though it was a little more difficult than usual, Liquid picked up another win on Saturday, beating Shopify Rebellion 2-1 to improve to 5-0 in the standings. In Saturday's other match, LYON swept Cloud 9. The LCS Summer Split is an eight-team event that began July 25 and will run through the finals in October. The seven-week round-robin regular season -- in which all teams play each other once in a best-of-three match -- will set the field for the six-team playoffs. The top two teams in the regular season will advance to the playoff semifinals, while the third- through sixth-place teams will advance to the quarters. The bottom two teams in the standings are eliminated. The playoffs, which run Sept. 12 through Oct. 4, are best-of-five and double elimination. The top three teams will advance to the World Championship, played in New York, Los Angeles and Allen, Texas, from Oct. 15 through Nov. 14. After winning their first four matches in sweeps, Liquid dropped their first map against Shopify, losing in 36 minutes. But Liquid rebounded to win the next two maps in 28 and 36 minutes. Sean "Yeon" Sung led Liquid with a 16/6/12 kill/death/assist ratio while South Korean Jo "CoreJJ" Yong-in posted 35 assists in the win. In the second match, LYON dominated from the get-go, winning in 47 and 35 minutes, respectively. In the balanced effort, Park "Thanatos" Seung-gyu of South Korea, Edward "Tactical" Ra and Lee "Loki" Sang-min of South Korea each averaged at least two kills per map. item.title: Orangutan rescued from fire zone in Indonesia's Borneo, battles respiratory illness
item.description: On Sunday morning, Jais, a farmer in Ketapang, West Kalimantan on Borneo island - the province hardest-hit by raging forest fires - was en route to his farm when he found an orangutan writhing on the ground in a weak state on a palm-oil plantation near the fire site.
item.dc:creator: Yuddy Budiman, Willy Kurniawan
item.content:encoded: On Sunday morning, Jais, a farmer in Ketapang, West [USN:L4N44I0DB TEXT:"Kalimantan"] on Borneo island - the province hardest-hit by raging forest fires - was en route to his farm when he found an orangutan writhing on the ground in a weak state on a palm-oil plantation near the fire site. "It was very weak, then I gave it water," said Jais, who only goes by one name. Indonesia has [USN:L1N448068 TEXT:"intensified"] efforts to contain haze from forest and land fires across six provinces in Borneo and Sumatra islands after smoke triggered respiratory illnesses and forced thousands of schools to move classes online, including in neighbouring [USN:L6N44L0EQ TEXT:"Malaysia"]. Wildfires burned at least 202,010 hectares (499,177.58 acres) of land from January to July, according to Indonesia's Forestry Ministry, increasing from 107,465 burned hectares from January to June. After finding the orangutan, Jais and other residents immediately called for help. Some two hours later, a wildlife foundation - Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia - arrived with a veterinarian to provide the animal with treatment. It had fainted by then. REUTERS/Willy Kurniawan The orangutan was then named Sampurna, after the village where it was found. Foundation CEO Karmele Llano Sanchez said the orangutan fainted because it did not get enough oxygen. "The orangutan got hypoxia because of the very thick smoke in the area," Sanchez told Reuters. Komara, the veterinarian, said the orangutan did not have any severe burn-related injuries. But it had breathing problems and had vomited. "We suspected it was suffering from an acute respiratory infection," he said, adding that the orangutan is around 20 years old. At the palm-oil plantation, the orangutan lay on a net, appearing weak with its eyes closed. The veterinarian gave the orangutan oxygen through small tubes placed in its nose. REUTERS/Willy Kurniawan Sampurna received fluids through an intravenous drip, with a makeshift infusion bag hanging from a palm-oil frond. The animal will be moved to a rehabilitation center to get more treatment, she said. It will be released back into the wild once it recovers, said Komara, adding that they have rescued seven orangutans due to fires so far. Sanchez warned that the government must not only focus on containing fires, but prepare for the long-term effects on public health, forests and wildlife.

item.content:encoded: Switzerland risks undermining its position as a global financial centre by imposing excessive regulation on its banks, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing an interview with the incoming head of the country's banking lobby Giorgio Pradelli. Pradelli, who is also the CEO of Zurich-based private bank EFG International (EFGN.S) , is set to take over as chair of the [USN:FWN41P03D TEXT:"Swiss Bankers Association"] next month while remaining CEO of EFG International. “We cannot take it for granted that Switzerland will always be prominent if we do not apply the right policies, including the regulatory framework,” he told the FT. In the coming days, a Swiss parliamentary committee will vote on proposed new banking regulations for UBS (UBSG.S) , after a prior panel failed to [USN:L8N4441DS TEXT:"strike"] a deal.

item.title: Nationals look to avenge last weekend's series sweep by Marlins
item.description: The Washington Nationals have a 6-12 record and have not won a series since they swept the Cincinnati Reds three weeks ago, but following back-to-back road wins over the Miami Marlins, the Nationals have a shot at success.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Washington Nationals have a 6-12 record and have not won a series since they swept the Cincinnati Reds three weeks ago, but following back-to-back road wins over the Miami Marlins, the Nationals have a shot at success. The Nationals will host the Marlins in the third contest of a four-game series on Sunday. A victory will give them their first series win since they took three games from the Reds from Aug. 7-9. The Nationals also could pay the Marlins back for their three-game sweep of Washington last week in Miami with wins both Sunday and Monday. Left-hander Andrew Alvarez (2-6, 3.72 ERA) will pitch for the Nationals, seeking to break his personal three-game losing streak. The Nationals scored just two total runs in those games -- a 3-1 setback to the Colorado Rockies on Tuesday, preceded by 2-0 and 4-1 losses to the Texas Rangers and New York Mets, respectively. Offense has not been a problem in the first two games in Miami for the Nationals, who won the opener 9-2 on Friday night and 5-4 in 10 innings on Saturday. And that reflects their season. The Nationals have scored 718 runs in 2026, trailing the MLB-leading Chicago Cubs by just two. On Saturday, the Nationals scored four runs in the third inning, and the Marlins tied the game with four runs in the seventh. In the 10th, Washington accomplished a season first -- a walk-off win -- when Dylan Crews' two-out, bases loaded single scored automatic runner Nasim Nunez from third. "That's an awesome win right there, what a dogfight," Crews said on the field after the game. " ... We've been going through it the past couple of weeks. With this team, we're never out of a game." The postgame enthusiasm likely was tempered a bit by the potential of an injury to starter Cade Cavalli, who was hit in the right calf by a comebacker off the bat of Javier Sanoja with two outs in the fourth inning. Cavalli recovered to throw out Sanoja to end the inning but did not return to pitch in the fifth. Cavalli has been the most consistent pitcher for the Nationals, holding the team lead in three categories with 12 wins, a 3.12 ERA and 177 strikeouts. In his four innings on Saturday, Cavalli gave up no hits, walked three and struck out eight. The Marlins have lost four of their past five games and had a shot to win on Saturday after they fought back from a 4-0 deficit, thanks to a two-run double by Kyle Stowers and a two-run home run by Heriberto Hernandez, both with two outs. It was the 22nd home run of the season -- a team high -- for Hernandez. He is the third Marlins' outfielder since 2018 with 20 home runs in a season, joining Stowers (2025) and Adam Duvall (2021). "Bert can hit, and one thing Bert can do is he can hit velocity, and he can hit in-zone spin, and he handles left-handers very well," manager Clayton McCullough said of Hernandez. Hernandez likely will be in the lineup Sunday against the left-handed Alvarez. Alvarez is 0-1 with an 0.93 ERA in two career starts against Miami. He most recently faced the Marlins on June 3, allowing one run on four hits and a walk in 4 2/3 innings. He struck out five batters and took a no-decision in the 4-1 loss. Right-hander Janson Junk (6-8, 4.21) is expected to start for the Marlins on Sunday, making his third appearance in eight days. If McCullough pivots because of the workload for Junk, it likely will be right-hander Tyler Phillips (3-6, 3.59) on the mound. Junk faced the Nationals just a week ago, giving up one run on two hits in 4 2/3 innings, throwing 69 pitches in the 6-2 victory last Sunday. He did not pitch enough innings to earn the win. With the Marlins in need of a spot reliever, Junk pitched one inning Wednesday, retiring the Boston Red Sox in order on just eight pitches in the eighth inning in the 4-0 Miami victory. In his career against Washington, Junk is 1-1 with a 4.79 ERA in four appearances (three starts). --Field Level Media

item.title: Malaysia PM unveils measures to tackle living costs, support local businesses
item.description: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Sunday introduced measures to address rising living costs and support businesses, including restoring higher quotas for subsidised petrol and diesel purchases, as well as more funding for schools and small traders.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Sunday introduced measures to address rising living costs and support businesses, including restoring higher quotas for subsidised petrol and diesel purchases, as well as more funding for schools and small traders. The measures are expected to take effect on September 1, Anwar said in a televised address. "The economic growth of the country must be returned to the people," he said. Anwar has been [USN:L4N3TM0Q2 TEXT:"under pressure"] to tackle higher living costs, even as Malaysia's economy has outperformed most of its regional peers. The country's gross domestic product [USN:L6N44B09V TEXT:"grew 6%"] in the second quarter this year, surpassing official projections. Anwar said the government would restore a quota for Malaysian citizens to buy the popular RON95 transport fuel to 300 litres per month, after [USN:L6N40E0E4 TEXT:"reducing"] it to 200 litres a month earlier this year amid a surge in global crude oil prices due to the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The quota for diesel purchases for certain categories of users would be similarly raised to 400 litres per month, he said. Anwar said a government artificial intelligence program would be opened to Malaysians aged between 18 and 30 years that would include free access to several key applications including Google's (GOOGL.O) Gemini Enterprise and Wonderclip and MuleRun by China's Alibaba Cloud. He also unveiled increased funding for maintaining schools, improving digital health systems and micro-financing facilities for small businesses. He said the government would raise the revenue threshold exempting companies from implementing e-invoicing to 3 million ringgit a year. Any funds seized or forfeited from anti-corruption legal proceedings would be channelled to government programs, particularly in education and healthcare, he added. Anwar's coalition has faced declining support over what critics have described as a failure to deliver on promised reforms and the mishandling of several [USN:L6N3ZT0B7 TEXT:"high-profile corruption cases"]. The coalition has been [USN:L6N44100V TEXT:"defeated"] in three successive regional elections in recent months. The state elections are widely seen as an indicator of voter sentiment ahead of a general election that must be held by early 2028. Anwar has said he [USN:L1N41U01T TEXT:"may call for snap polls"] if divisions within his administration continue to widen. ($1 = 4.0220 ringgit)

item.title: India's HDFC Bank weighing deputy MD Bharucha, outsider for CEO, sources say
item.description: HDFC Bank is likely to name Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha as one of two options for its next CEO after incumbent Sashidhar Jagdishan retires at the end of his second term in October, two people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Gopika Gopakumar
item.content:encoded: HDFC Bank (HDBK.NS) is likely to name Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha as one of two options for its next CEO after incumbent Sashidhar Jagdishan retires at the end of his second term in October, two people familiar with the matter said. India's largest private lender is also searching for an external candidate in keeping with a central bank rule requiring banks submit multiple names for the CEO position, the people said, declining to be identified as the information was private. The Reserve Bank of India approves top banking appointments. Neither HDFC Bank nor Bharucha responded to emails seeking comment outside of regular business hours. The CEO search comes after about six months of upheaval at HDFC Bank where leadership issues have weighed on its shares. The bank announced Jagdishan's [USN:L1N44Q03M TEXT:"retirement"] on Saturday. He had been widely tipped to continue as CEO before Atanu Chakraborty resigned as chairman in March saying practices at the bank were at odds with his "personal values and ethics". An external legal review found [USN:L4N42Y132 TEXT:"no evidence"] to substantiate Chakraborty's governance concerns. Last month, the board [USN:L4N43T0QY TEXT:"penalised"] Jagdishan and three others in a separate matter related to the pricing of large deposits. The bank said on Saturday without elaborating that its CEO since October 2020 had decided not to seek reappointment and that it would fast-track the appointment of a successor. Among the leading internal candidates is Bharucha, a long-serving executive overseeing the retail and wholesale businesses, the people said. Bharucha is not due to retire until 2029, when he will have been a full-time director for 15 years, making him eligible to be CEO under RBI rules. The maximum tenure of a so-called whole-time director is 15 years, though exemptions can be sought. The price of HDFC Bank shares, which were about 40% foreign-owned as at June-end, has fallen 27% this year, with the decline accelerating after Chakraborty's departure. Investors have also [USN:L4N40B0WF TEXT:"voiced concern"] over the lack of gains from a 2023 merger overseen by Jagdishan with then-parent HDFC Ltd.

item.title: Iran's Khamenei urges Gulf rulers in written message to confront 'real enemy'
item.description: Iran's supreme leader posted a written message on Telegram. He has not been seen in months.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei urged Muslim countries, particularly those in the Gulf, to unite against what he called their "real enemy" and said divisions among Muslims served the interests of their adversaries. The message was published on Khamenei's Telegram account for Islamic Unity Week, which marks the birthday of the Prophet Muhammad. It called for Muslim unity, cooperation in various fields and mutual defence, saying anyone who creates divisions among Muslims, "knowingly or unknowingly," helps Islam's enemies. It asked whether Palestinians would have been left "so helpless" if Muslims had been united. Khamenei has not been seen in public since being injured in U.S.-Israeli airstrikes six months ago that launched the Iran war, killing his father and previous supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. His call for unity echoes a statement he made [USN:S8N42F04N TEXT:"on Friday to Iranians"], when he said he had banned actions that harm social cohesion and urged authorities to avoid "discouraging statements" that weaken national and public morale. Khamenei specifically asked Gulf Arab rulers whether "rogues without identity" would have dared to covet their lands and possessions if the peoples and governments of the Gulf had been "united under the flag of Islam." Since the 1979 Islamic Revolution, Gulf Arab monarchies have viewed Iran's revolutionary ideology, including its anti-monarchic rhetoric and regional influence, as a threat to their political systems. During the present conflict, Tehran has struck U.S. military facilities as well as other infrastructure in Gulf states, underscoring the tensions between Tehran and its Gulf neighbours. "My emphatic and repeated recommendation to the rulers of Islamic countries, especially the countries of West Asia and the Gulf, is to identify your real enemy, understand his plan and confront it," Khamenei said.

item.title: MLB roundup: Pete Crow-Armstrong (3 HRs), Cubs overpower Reds
item.description: Pete Crow-Armstrong recorded his first three-homer game and drove in six runs to power the host Chicago Cubs to a 17-5 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pete Crow-Armstrong recorded his first three-homer game and drove in six runs to power the host Chicago Cubs to a 17-5 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Saturday. Crow-Armstrong increased his team-leading homer total to 36 with a solo shot in the first inning, a two-run blast in the second and a three-run homer in the seventh. Carson Kelly added a three-run homer and an RBI double for Chicago. Seiya Suzuki belted a two-run homer while Alex Bregman also went deep and added an RBI single as both players finished with three hits. Tyrone Taylor matched Crow-Armstrong with four of the Cubs' 19 hits and Nico Hoerner added an RBI single to help the team snap a three-game losing skid. The power display backed Kevin Gausman (8-11), who allowed five runs on six hits in five innings. Cincinnati rookie Sal Stewart belted a two-run shot for his team-leading 30th homer of the season. Eugenio Suarez also had a two-run homer and JJ Bleday added a sacrifice fly for the Reds, who lost for the 10th time in 15 games. Red Sox 6, Yankees 0 (Game 1) Rookie Jake Bennett pitched six strong innings and visiting Boston piled on during a four-run ninth inning against New York. Bennett (9-6) allowed three hits in his fourth career scoreless start. He struck out seven without a walk and has allowed one run on six hits in 12 1/3 innings during his two starts against the Yankees. Wilyer Abreu homered in the first inning against New York starter Carlos Rodon (4-3), Adley Rutschman enjoyed his first three-hit game with the Red Sox and Andruw Monasterio added a two-run double to lead Boston. Yankees 9, Red Sox 2 (Game 2) Ben Rice capped New York's five-run eighth inning with a two-run single during a three-RBI night as it evened the season series with a doubleheader split against visiting Boston. The Yankees had seven hits in the eighth and 13 in the game after totaling just seven across the first two games of the series. New York actually took control during a three-run third inning off Brayan Bello (5-7). With the win, the Yankees moved three games ahead of the Red Sox for the American League's top wild-card spot. New York starter Max Fried held Boston to one run on three hits in 3 2/3 innings in his return from the injured list due to a bone bruise in his left elbow. Mets 6, Astros 2 Nolan McLean tossed seven innings of two-hit ball and earned the win for host New York, which beat Houston in the middle contest of a three-game interleague series. Juan Soto returned from the injured list after sitting out five weeks due to strained left calf and went 1-for-4 with the tiebreaking RBI single in the fifth for the Mets. Jared Young had three hits and three RBIs, including a two-run triple to close out the fifth-inning rally, as New York improved to 14-11 this month. Yordan Alvarez homered and had a sacrifice fly for the American League West-leading Astros, who fell to 3-2 on their New York road trip. White Sox 3, Twins 2 Andrew Benintendi went 3-for-4 with a double, a homer and two RBIs in Minneapolis as Chicago extended its win streak to four games. Benintendi's three hits marked the only hits of the day for the White Sox. Josh Bell and Walker Jenkins each went 1-for-3 with an RBI for the Twins and Luke Keaschall added a double. Chicago right-hander Erick Fedde (7-8) earned the win after holding Minnesota to two runs on three hits in five innings. Jenkins notched his first career RBI on a groundout in the second inning. Tigers 2, Dodgers 1 Kevin McGonigle delivered a bases-loaded single in the ninth to drive in the winning run as host Detroit edged Los Angeles to even their three-game series. Javier Baez scored both runs for the Tigers, who had lost eight of their previous nine games. Gleyber Torres drove in the other run for Detroit. Kenley Jansen (4-5) picked up the win in relief. Starter Keider Montero gave up one run and four hits in 5 1/3 innings. Freddie Freeman drove in the lone run as the Dodgers lost for the fourth time in five games. The loss spoiled a strong outing by starter Blake Snell, who gave up one run and three hits in five innings while striking out 10. Nationals 5, Marlins 4 (10 innings) Dylan Crews' two-out bases-loaded single in the 10th lifted host Washington to its first walk-off win of the season. Crews lined an 0-1 four-seam fastball from Michael Petersen (3-4) into right-center field for his first career walk-off hit. Heriberto Hernandez homered for Miami, which has lost four of its last five. Nationals starter Cade Cavalli left the game after taking a liner off his right calf with two out in the fourth. He recovered to throw Javier Sanoja out at first to end the half inning but limped to the dugout. Braves 2, Rockies 1 Michael Harris II laced a go-ahead two-run double in the eighth inning to help streaking Atlanta top visiting Colorado for its sixth straight win. Brent Suter (2-2) threw 2 1/3 scoreless innings for the Braves, while Jaden Hill (0-3) took the loss after allowing Harris' double among three hits in his one-inning relief appearance. Willi Castro plated the Rockies' lone run on a two-out run-scoring single in the sixth. Colorado's Ryan Feltner was scratched from his scheduled start due to illness. Blue Jays 4, Mariners 3 Alejandro Kirk singled in the go-ahead run in a two-run sixth, Jose Soriano pitched seven effective innings and host Toronto defeated Seattle. Soriano (11-7) allowed three runs, five hits and two walks while striking out six. Louis Varland pitched the ninth to earn his 31st save. Cal Raleigh hit a solo home run for the Mariners, who led 3-0 after four innings. The Blue Jays took a 4-3 lead in the sixth against Jose Ferrer (4-3). Charles McAdoo and Myles Straw walked. Brett Bateman grounded an RBI single with two outs that found a hole through the left side of the infield. Kirk's single to right scored the go-ahead run. Pirates 6, Cardinals 2 Rookie slugger Rafael Flores Jr. hit a three-run home run for visiting Pittsburgh, which effectively used six pitchers in a bullpen game to beat St. Louis and even their three-game series. Brandon Lowe added a solo homer in the first inning for the Pirates, who overcame three straight errors at one point in the game. Right-hander Carmen Mlodzinski (7-6) earned the victory by allowing an unearned run and one hit in 3 1/3 relief innings. Jacob Gonzalez hit a tie-breaking RBI single in the fourth and Flores made it 5-1 with two outs in the fifth with his seventh homer of the season off left-hander Brycen Mautz (0-1). Diamondbacks 7, Giants 1 (Game 1) Merrill Kelly combined with two relievers on a four-hitter, Lars Nootbaar broke a scoreless deadlock with a seventh-inning, pinch-hit grand slam and Arizona beat San Francisco in the opener of a day-night doubleheader. Kelly (9-12) called it a day after seven shutout innings in which he allowed just a pair of singles and four walks. The right-hander struck out seven. Brandyn Garcia wrapped up the Diamondbacks' seventh win in their last 10 games with a 1-2-3 ninth. Making his third big-league start, Giants rookie left-hander Matt Wilkinson (0-2) was charged with two of the runs. He limited Arizona to three hits in his six-plus innings, with two walks and four strikeouts. Giants 7, Diamondbacks 2 (Game 2) Bryce Eldridge matched career highs with four hits and four RBIs, Rafael Devers drove in two runs with a pair of singles, and host San Francisco salvaged a doubleheader split with Arizona in the nightcap. Making his major league debut after a promotion from Double-A Richmond, Giants right-hander Yunior Marte worked 4 2/3 innings, limiting the Diamondbacks to one run and three hits. Reiver Sanmartin (2-0), who relieved Marte with two outs in the fifth with the game tied at 1-1, was credited with the win after facing just one batter, striking out Game 1 hero Lars Nootbaar. Arizona rookie left-hander Mitch Bratt (1-3) was charged with three runs on three hits in 4 1/3 innings. Royals 8, Guardians 3 Josh Rojas hit a two-run homer and tied his career high with four RBIs as surging Kansas City scored eight unanswered runs to beat host Cleveland and clinch a series win. Rojas had a two-run single in the sixth inning and added a two-run homer in the eighth to lift the Royals to their 12th win in 13 games. Royals reliever Anthony Gose (1-0) retired all five batters he faced to collect his first victory since June 17, 2022, while pitching for the Guardians. Cleveland reliever Colin Holderman (6-4) took the loss after recording only one out. He was charged with four runs (three earned) during Kansas City's breakout sixth. Angel Martinez had a two-run homer off starter Daniel Lynch IV for the Guardians. Rays 7, Padres 6 Chandler Simpson slashed a tiebreaking, two-out single to cap a four-run, seventh-inning rally, lifting Tampa Bay to a wild win and a series victory over San Diego in St. Petersburg, Fla. The Rays' Jonathan Aranda hit a tape-measure home run, and Junior Caminero ripped his 36th to tie Houston's Yordan Alvarez for the American League lead. Starting pitcher Nick Martinez allowed three runs on seven hits in six innings with four strikeouts and no walks. Reliever Kevin Kelly (6-3) pitched 1 2/3 scoreless innings, while Bryan Baker recorded his 39th save. The Padres' Dustin Harris had three hits, two runs and a stolen base. Ty France had two hits, including his 100th career homer. Manny Machado had two hits and two RBIs. Bradgley Rodriguez (3-3) allowed four runs (one earned) on three hits and a walk without retiring a batter. Orioles 5, Athletics 3 Leody Taveras doubled twice and drove in three runs as Baltimore downed the Athletics in West Sacramento, Calif. Colton Cowser homered and scored two runs in the second game of the three-game series and Coby Mayo also scored twice for the Orioles. Right-hander Shane Baz (5-14) ended a five-start losing streak by limiting the Athletics to two runs and five hits over 5 2/3 innings. He struck out four and walked three. Seeking his second straight win, A's starter Jack Perkins (3-10) limited Baltimore to two runs (one earned) and four hits over five innings. The right-hander struck out five and walked four. Carlos Cortes had two hits and an RBI, and Jeff McNeil had two hits and scored a run for the A's. Brewers 5, Rangers 3 Jackson Chourio and William Contreras each homered in the first inning and Shane Drohan tossed five solid innings for host Milwaukee, which beat Texas for its fourth straight win. Drohan (7-5) allowed one run on six hits with one walk and six strikeouts for his first victory since July 31. Luis Lara had two hits and two RBIs for Milwaukee, which won its fourth straight. Brandon Nimmo hit a two-run homer as part of a three-hit game for the Rangers, and teammate Cody Freeman went deep for the first time this season. Phillies 4, Angels 2 (10 innings) Kyle Schwarber drove in the go-ahead run with a bloop double and Trea Turner added a two-run single to highlight a three-run 10th inning and lead Philadelphia over Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif. Alec Bohm went 2-for-4 with a run scored and Turner had two hits and two RBIs for Philadelphia, which won for the 12th time in its last 14 games. Jhoan Duran (2-4) picked up the win, allowing one unearned run in two innings of relief. Zach Neto hit a home run for Los Angeles, which finished with just four hits while losing its sixth straight game. Right-hander Trevor Martin (0-1), making his Angels debut after being claimed on waivers from Tampa Bay on Aug. 15, picked up the loss. --Field Level Media
