item.title: Venezuela's interim president says US energy deal will last 25 years
item.description: The deal would target an increase in crude output to 1.5 million barrels per day and preserve Venezuela's sovereignty over its natural resources, Delcy Rodríguez said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez said on Saturday that an energy agreement with the [USN:FWN44P1ZC TEXT:"U.S."] would remain in force for 25 years, target an increase in crude output to 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) and preserve the country's sovereignty over its natural resources. Rodriguez hailed the accord in a late-night address as a "historic" deal that would help revive the economy and boost government revenue, saying it would help shape the country's future. “This 25-year bilateral project envisages the development of 17 strategic oilfields with a production target of more than 1.5 million barrels per day," Rodriguez said on state broadcaster VTV. "That figure relates solely to the bilateral agreement between Venezuela and the United States." Rodriguez added that the agreement's target of 1.5 million bpd was only an initial goal and that the broader plan also included the development of eight greenfield oil blocks as part of a wider expansion of the country's energy sector. President Donald Trump on Friday announced plans for the U.S. to take partial control of Venezuela's vast oil reserves, betting that American companies can help revive the South American nation's battered energy industry while providing a new source of crude to help lower U.S. fuel prices. Trump provided few details on the agreement, saying only that the U.S. had secured majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's proven oil reserves through a partnership with private business. Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves, but it produces only about 1.25 million bpd - far below its potential - after years of underinvestment, mismanagement and sanctions. Rodriguez said the agreement could generate about $209 billion in revenue for the Venezuelan state, based on a benchmark oil price of $65 per barrel, though she acknowledged crude prices could fluctuate. She said roughly $19 from each barrel produced and sold under the arrangement would flow directly to Venezuela, providing a significant boost to government revenue. She said that the country retained “ownership of and sovereignty” over its natural resources, “while leveraging capital, technology and operational expertise to support the recovery of a strategic industry that has been severely affected by sanctions." Earlier on Saturday, dozens of pro-government groups gathered in downtown Caracas to protest against the U.S. presence in Venezuela. Rodriguez welcomed the agreement following Trump's announcement, saying it would bolster economic growth and increase government revenue. Venezuelan officials are preparing to sign agreements next week granting new oil exploration and production rights to several companies, including U.S. firms. Two sources close to the negotiations said on Friday that [USN:L6N44P13H TEXT:"Chevron CVX.N was among the companies"] expected to finalize talks to transition its Venezuelan joint ventures into the country's new energy framework.

item.title: Presidenta encargada de Venezuela dice que acuerdo petrolero con EEUU será por 25 años
item.description: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, dijo el sábado que el acuerdo petrolero con Estados Unidos se mantendrá vigente durante 25 años con el objetivo de aumentar inicialmente la producción de crudo a 1,5 millones de barriles diarios, agregando que el país sudamericano mantiene la soberanía sobre sus recursos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, dijo el sábado que el acuerdo petrolero con Estados Unidos se mantendrá vigente durante 25 años con el objetivo de aumentar inicialmente la producción de crudo a 1,5 millones de barriles diarios, agregando que el país sudamericano mantiene la soberanía sobre sus recursos. Rodríguez elogió el acuerdo con Washington en un discurso transmitido por la televisión estatal en horas de la noche y lo calificó de "histórico", porque reactivará la economía y aumentará los ingresos del gobierno. "Este proyecto binacional, suscrito por 25 años, contempla el desarrollo de 17 campos estratégicos con un objetivo de producción superior a 1,5 millones de barriles diarios. Esto solamente con el acuerdo binacional Venezuela-Estados Unidos, pero nuestra meta va más allá", agregó Rodríguez, quien señaló que el proyecto contempla el desarrollo de ocho campos verdes (greenfields) en la Faja del Orinoco. El viernes, el presidente Donald Trump [USN:L6N44Q004 TEXT:"anunció"] planes para que Estados Unidos tome el control parcial de las vastas reservas petroleras de Venezuela, apostando a que las empresas estadounidenses pueden ayudar a reactivar la maltrecha industria energética del país miembro de la OPEP, a la vez que proporcionan una nueva fuente de crudo para ayudar a reducir los precios del combustible en Estados Unidos. Trump ofreció pocos detalles sobre el acuerdo, limitándose a decir que Estados Unidos había asegurado el control mayoritario de más de 65.000 millones de barriles de las reservas probadas de petróleo de Venezuela mediante una alianza con empresas privadas. "Tomando como referencia un precio de 65 dólares por barril (...) los ingresos de nuestro país llegarían a un total de 209.335 millones de dólares para el Estado venezolano. En términos concretos, esto significa que por cada barril producido y vendido cerca de 19 dólares ingresan directamente a nuestro país", añadió Rodríguez, sin más detalles. Venezuela posee las mayores reservas probadas de petróleo del mundo, pero produce solo alrededor de 1,25 millones de barriles diarios, muy por debajo de su potencial tras años de baja inversión, mala gestión y sanciones. Tras agradecer al presidente Trump y al secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, los esfuerzos por el acuerdo, la presidenta encargada dijo que Venezuela mantiene la soberanía sobre sus recursos naturales. "Venezuela conserva la propiedad y la soberanía sobre sus recursos, mientras utiliza capital, tecnología y capacidad operativa para apalancar la recuperación de una industria estratégica duramente golpeada por sanciones", añadió. Funcionarios venezolanos se preparan para firmar la próxima semana acuerdos que otorgarán nuevos derechos de exploración y producción de petróleo a varias empresas, en particular a firmas estadounidenses. Dos fuentes indicaron el viernes que [USN:L6N44P13Z TEXT:"Chevron"] figuraba entre las petroleras que finalizarían las negociaciones para integrar todas sus empresas mixtas en Venezuela al nuevo marco energético del país.

item.title: Brewers get early HRs, strong outing from Shane Drohan to top Rangers
item.description: Jackson Chourio and William Contreras each homered in the first inning and Shane Drohan tossed five solid innings as the Milwaukee Brewers beat the visiting Texas Rangers 5-3 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jackson Chourio and William Contreras each homered in the first inning and Shane Drohan tossed five solid innings as the Milwaukee Brewers beat the visiting Texas Rangers 5-3 on Saturday. Drohan (7-5) allowed one run on six hits with one walk and six strikeouts for his first victory since July 31. Luis Lara had two hits and two RBIs for Milwaukee, which won its fourth straight. The Rangers trailed 5-1 with one out in the eighth inning before pulling closer on Brandon Nimmo's two-run homer against Chad Patrick. Antonio Senzatela replaced Patrick and allowed Ezequiel Duran's single before retiring the next two batters. Trevor Megill pitched a scoreless ninth for his 25th save. Cody Freeman hit a solo homer and Nimmo had three hits for Texas, which lost its fourth straight. Milwaukee claimed a 2-0 lead in the first inning against Cal Quantrill (6-5) on a pair of solo homers by Chourio and Contreras. Chourio's one-out shot over the center field wall was his third homer in his last three games and his 20th of the season. After Jake Bauers struck out, Contreras turned on Quantrill's 2-2 sinker for his 13th homer of the year. The Brewers tacked on a run in the second inning. Christian Yelich hit a leadoff double, stole third, and scored on Lara's liner into center field. Lara was thrown out on the play while attempting to stretch the single into a double. Texas got on the board when Freeman began the fifth inning with his first homer of the season. Quantrill was replaced by Peyton Gray after allowing three runs on four hits with no walks and a season-high eight strikeouts over six innings. He retired the final 14 batters he faced. Milwaukee extended its lead with two runs against Gray in the seventh. With the bases loaded and no outs, Lara singled in a run and another run scored on Cooper Pratt's sacrifice fly. The Brewers loaded the bases with two outs in the eighth, but Jakob Junis struck out Lara to escape the jam. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tyson Bagent, Bears blitz Titans, 24-15
item.description: Bears backup quarterback Tyson Bagent and wide receiver Zavion Thomas connected on a 97-yard touchdown on Chicago's opening play and didn't stop there in a 24-15 win over the Titans in Nashville on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Bears backup quarterback Tyson Bagent and wide receiver Zavion Thomas connected on a 97-yard touchdown on Chicago's opening play and didn't stop there in a 24-15 win over the Titans in Nashville on Saturday. Thomas, a rookie third-round pick, made his preseason debut and racked up 140 yards on five receptions with a 39-yard punt return. Bagent was almost perfect as a passer -- he completed 16 of 17 throws for 208 yards and two touchdowns -- and the Bears (2-1) overcame his fumble on a busted run play in a game that featured mostly reserves in the closing preseason action for both clubs. On first down from their own 3, Bagent dropped back into the end zone and locked onto Thomas split wide to his right. Thomas hesitated and the Titans' secondary froze. With the pocket shrinking around him, Bagent let the ball go as Thomas, who was the third-fastest player timed at the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine, shifted gears. He came back for the underthrown pass, then burst into the open, sprinting down the sideline for the touchdown. Bears wide receiver Maurice Alexander caught Bagent's other TD toss and had a game-high seven receptions for 50 yards. The Bears led 14-9 at halftime. Chicago added Roschon Johnson's 3-yard touchdown run and a Cairo Santos field goal in the third quarter to push their lead to 24-9. Johnson had 15 carries for 52 yards. With starting quarterback Cam Ward and backup Mitch Trubisky rested, quarterback Will Levis, fighting for a roster spot ahead of NFL cuts, started for the Titans. He played the entire first half and led three scoring drives (all field goals). Running back D'Ernest Johnson scored Tennessee's only touchdown on a 9-yard run with 3:50 to play and celebrated with the "Choppa City Juke," an homage to former Titans running back Chris Johnson. Titans kicker Joey Slye made all three of his field goal tries, including a 56-yarder, his fifth this preseason of at least 50 yards. --Field Level Media

item.title: US to take 35% stake in Venezuelan mogul Betancourt's oil venture, WSJ reports
item.description: The U.S. plans to secure preferential rights to purchase 20% of the company's production.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. government plans to take a 35% passive stake in Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt’s North American Blue Energy Partners, the Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing people involved in negotiating the deal. The U.S. also plans to secure preferential rights to purchase 20% of the company's production at cost, the WSJ reported. The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital plans to structure the investment through penny warrants that would yield the U.S. an equity ownership in the business without significant capital investment, the WSJ reported. The report comes only a day after U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday that the U.S. would take control of a [USN:FWN44P1ZC TEXT:"fifth"] of Venezuela's vast oil reserves. Trump provided few details about the arrangement, saying only that the U.S. had secured majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's proven oil reserves through a partnership with private business. Responding to a Reuters request for comment, chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said: "The Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) does not take equity stakes in private companies. Under its statutory authority, OSC's role is strictly limited to providing capital assistance in the form of a loan, loan guarantee, or technical assistance (including transaction structuring for developing and financing investments)." The White House and North American Blue Energy Partners did not respond to requests for comments outside regular business hours.

item.title: President Donald Trump to attend Presidents Cup
item.description: President Donald Trump will serve as the honorary chairman at the 2026 Presidents Cup and plans to attend the event that will be held at Medinah Country Club in Chicago from Sept. 24-27.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump will serve as the honorary chairman at the 2026 Presidents Cup and plans to attend the event that will be held at Medinah Country Club in Chicago from Sept. 24-27. "At the request of the PGA Tour, and its Great new Commissioner, Brian Rolapp, it is my Honor to accept being the Honorary Chairman of the upcoming Presidents Cup, which will take place at the Medinah Country Club in Chicago," Trump said in a statement posted on Truth Social. "This will be a particularly exciting event. Both teams are "loaded" with Talent. I look forward to being there, and greeting all of these fantastic athletes, on both teams! Thank you for your attention to this matter. See you in Chicago! Trump served the same role for the 2017 Presidents Cup held at Liberty National Golf Club in New Jersey during his first presidential term. The U.S. won that competition over the international team, 19-11. He also made an appearance during the first round at last year's Ryder Cup held at Bethpage Black on Long Island. "The Presidents Cup has a proud tradition of engaging world leaders from across the globe and across political lines, and President Trump's involvement continues that legacy," PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said in a statement. "His participation will help elevate the event on the international stage while furthering our mission of bringing people together through the game of golf." Brandt Snedeker will serve as captain of the American team that will take on an international team led by captain Geoff Ogilvy of Australia next month. Trump joins six former presidents to serve as the honorary chairman for the event: Joe Biden, Barack Obama, George W. Bush, Bill Clinton, George H.W. Bush and Gerald Ford. Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau took part in the trophy presentation at the most recent Presidents Cup at Royal Montreal in 2024. Other world leaders who have held the position include Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison and South Korean President Park Geun-hye. --Field Level Media

item.title: Emotional Federer full of love and gratitude at Hall of Fame induction
item.description: An emotional Roger Federer said he was still writing his love letter to the sport that "meant the world" to him on Saturday as the 20-time Grand Slam champion was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in Newport, Rhode Island.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An emotional Roger Federer said he was still writing his love letter to the sport that "meant the world" to him on Saturday as the 20-time Grand Slam champion was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in Newport, Rhode Island. Federer, who was inducted alongside broadcaster and journalist Mary Carillo, reflected on his storied career in a speech that brought him to tears a few times. "This is one of the greatest honours of my life," said Federer. "They call this the Hall of Fame, but fame was never the goal. "My goal was to spend my life doing something I love ... with people who love it as much as I do." The Swiss captured a men's-record eight Wimbledon titles and spent 310 weeks as the world number one. He also won six Australian Open crowns, five U.S. Open titles and one French Open title. And he did it all while playing with elegance, a signature headband – apparently wearing more than 5,000 of them during his career, he quipped in his address – and almost always two pairs of socks. "Tennis meant the world to me. Not just playing, not just winning, but creating something new," said Federer, who retired in 2022 with 103 ATP Tour titles. "It's a mentality I have. I used to play serve and volley, I had a transition game, I played way beyond the baseline sometimes, or on top of the baseline. And I would even try to sneak up on my opponents on my return, and some call it the SABR (Sneak Attack by Roger) today. "This is what was important to me on the court, but so much of what was really important happened off the court." The 45-year-old got emotional while thanking his coaches, doctors and family, including wife Mirka, who praised Federer for his character off the court as husband, father and friend. As his name entered the Hall of Fame, Federer said he was proud that Switzerland was coming with him, recalling how he loved watching tennis as a 13-year-old ball boy in Basel. "I'm still writing my love letter to tennis, and my time as a player is done, but tennis will always stand at the intersection of everything I care most about," he said. "My family, our friendships, the past 40 years, the future we're building – tennis, for me, is responsible for it all. So this is not a goodbye." The Swiss said he was "incredibly lucky" to have played with different generations of tennis players, from Andre Agassi and Lleyton Hewitt to Andy Roddick, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic. But he added that his induction was not only an opportunity to look back on his career, but also ahead to the future of the game. "We all leave the court eventually, but the sport keeps evolving," said Federer. "And as the pace of professional tennis speeds up, as the sport becomes even more global, I so hope it will keep some of that amateur spirit. Keep the camaraderie among the players. "I hope the players will stay young at heart and stay true to their authentic selves, and always remember, never stop asking questions or taking risks. "Do things with the game, we've never seen before. Keep pushing this sport we love to the next level and keep getting better, better, and better."

item.title: Yankees SS George Lombard Jr. (knee) makes early exit vs. Red Sox
item.description: The New York Yankees removed rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. from the nightcap of their doubleheader with the visiting Boston Red Sox on Saturday night due to right knee discomfort.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New York Yankees removed rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. from the nightcap of their doubleheader with the visiting Boston Red Sox on Saturday night due to right knee discomfort. The team said Lombard was undergoing imaging at New York-Presbyterian Hospital. In the second inning, Lombard checked his swing on a pitch from Brayan Bello. Afterward, Lombard grimaced and held his right knee. After a team athletic trainer and manager Aaron Boone checked on him, Lombard stayed in the game and singled. Lombard batted in the third and flew out to left field after the Yankees took a 3-1 lead but was lifted for the start of the fourth inning. New York moved Jose Caballero from third base to shortstop and Amed Rosario entered the game at third. Lombard joined the team on Aug. 4 and was the first Yankees shortstop to homer in his major league debut. The 21-year-old is batting .253 with two homers and six RBIs in 23 games since getting promoted from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre. --Field Level Media

item.title: Reports: Cowboys acquire Steelers '23 first-rounder Broderick Jones
item.description: Offensive tackle Broderick Jones is being acquired by the Dallas Cowboys, who agreed to a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Saturday that includes three 2027 draft picks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Offensive tackle Broderick Jones is being acquired by the Dallas Cowboys, who agreed to a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Saturday that includes three 2027 draft picks. ESPN reported the trade agreement in place, pending a physical, sends Jones and a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Cowboys for third- and sixth-round picks in 2027. Jones, the Steelers' first-round pick in 2023, made 38 starts over three years but was working with the reserves in Pittsburgh during the preseason. He played both tackle spots in Pittsburgh. The Steelers drafted Max Iheanachor at No. 21 overall in April to play right tackle. He has been competing there with fifth-year veteran Dylan Cook while 2024 first-round pick Troy Fautanu has worked at left tackle. Former Cowboys coach Mike McCarthy, familiar with that organization's preference for a well-stocked offensive line, is entering his first season as Steelers coach. Terence Steele was the primary right tackle for the Cowboys last season. Dallas has been pleased with 2024 first-round pick Tyler Guyton at left tackle in the preseason. If Jones winds up taking over at right tackle, Dallas could start four first-round picks around center Cooper Beebe. --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: Mets place OF Luis Robert Jr. on waivers
item.description: The New York Mets placed outfielder Luis Robert Jr. on waivers, per MLB.com.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New York Mets placed outfielder Luis Robert Jr. on waivers, per MLB.com. The former All-Star, who pinch-hit during the Mets' 6-2 win over the Houston Astros on Saturday, has posted 10 home runs and 23 RBIs with a .229/.308/.407 slash line in 57 games this season. Those numbers include a strong push in August as he has amassed six home runs and 11 RBIs with a .282/.338/.557 line over 23 games. His ability to play center field could make him appealing to contenders, as well. Robert was an All-Star in 2023 with the Chicago White Sox, blasting 38 home runs and stealing 20 bases. However, injuries and inconsistency have hampered his production and value. The 29-year-old is owed roughly $3 million for the rest of this season. He also carries a $20 million club option for next season, though there's a $2 million buyout. With the Mets out of playoff contention, it is not surprising to see them trying to shed some salary. --Field Level Media

item.title: Pajari heading for third win in a row
item.description: Toyota's Sami Pajari was heading for his third win in a row after ending the penultimate leg of Rally Paraguay with a 24.1-second lead on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Toyota's Sami Pajari was heading for his third win in a row after ending the penultimate leg of Rally Paraguay with a 24.1-second lead on Saturday. The Finn, winner in Estonia and Finland, had been 11.9 seconds clear of New Zealander Hayden Paddon at the start of the day and managed his tyres to stretch his advantage over the largely dry day's nine stages to move within five of victory. "For me this is a different challenge than Estonia and Finland," said Pajari, who lost part of his rear wing when he ran wide in stage 11. "It is more about surviving. Many things can go wrong still tomorrow." Hyundai's Paddon ended the day 32.2 seconds clear of Toyota's world championship leader Elfyn Evans with Hyundai's Adrien Fourmaux challenging for the podium in fourth after winning five stages and closing the gap to 3.3 seconds after starting Saturday 55 seconds behind. Welshman Evans said Fourmaux, a distant sixth in the standings, was able to take risks because he had less to lose than others. “Adrien, to be fair, has been in a different rally to everyone else,” he said. “He is risking everything, but let’s see tomorrow.” Evans leads Pajari by 30 points in the standings with three rounds remaining after Paraguay.

item.title: Ethiopian Gobena and Kenya's Jepchirchir take Sydney marathon honours
item.description: Gobena crossed the line at the city's Opera House in two hours, four minutes and 42 seconds.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ethiopian Addisu Gobena smashed the course record to win the men's title before Kenya's world and former Olympic champion Peres Jepchirchir dominated the women's race at the Sydney Marathon on the penultimate day of the Australian winter on Sunday. Gobena, second last year, crossed the line at the city's Opera House in two hours, four minutes and 42 seconds, well clear of the previous record of 2:06:06 that his compatriot Hailemaryam Kiros clocked to win the race last year. Chimdessa Debele of Ethiopia was second in 2:04:46 with Lesotho’s Tebello Ramakongoana third in 2:04:57. “I am very happy," said 21-year-old Gobena, who broke clear of the five-strong leading pack in the closing stages to record the fastest-ever marathon time on Australian soil. "Last year I came second, I learnt from my mistake, and I went back home and I worked on my mistake to perform and broke the record today.” Jepchirchir blew away the field in the women's race, finishing more than three minutes clear of second-placed compatriot Irine Cheptai in 2:18:31 to win her fourth marathon major. Cheptai ran a time of 2:22:11 in perfect running conditions, while Ethiopian Shure Demise was third in 2:22:33. The 32-year-old Jepchirchir, who won Olympic gold in Tokyo in 2021, came up just short of the course record of 2:18:22 that current Olympic champion Sifan Hassan ran to win the Sydney race last year.

item.title: Michael Harris II's clutch double enables Braves to drop Rockies
item.description: Michael Harris II laced a go-ahead two-run double in the eighth inning on Saturday to help the streaking Atlanta Braves earn a 2-1 victory over the visiting Colorado Rockies.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Michael Harris II laced a go-ahead two-run double in the eighth inning on Saturday to help the streaking Atlanta Braves earn a 2-1 victory over the visiting Colorado Rockies. Atlanta mounted a two-out rally in the eighth. Colorado reliever Jaden Hill (0-3) allowed singles by Matt Olson and Mauricio Dubon before Harris split the left-center gap with the Braves' lone extra-base hit. Didier Fuentes handled the ninth for the Braves. After issuing a leadoff walk to Willi Castro and allowing a one-out single to Troy Johnston, the 21-year-old Fuentes struck out Zac Veen and got Jake McCarthy to line out to seal his third save and Atlanta's sixth straight win. Brent Suter (2-2) threw 2 1/3 scoreless innings for the Braves. Colorado's Ryan Feltner was scratched from his scheduled start due to illness. In his place, Zach Agnos opened with 2 2/3 scoreless innings. Six pitchers combined to allow six Atlanta hits. After the first pitch was delayed 15 minutes by rain, Martin Perez started strongly. Before allowing Cole Carrigg's two-out double in the third, he fanned five straight batters. Drake Baldwin and Ronald Acuna Jr. laced back-to-back two-out singles in the bottom of the third to chase Agnos after 42 pitches. Rookie Nick Frasso entered in relief and walked Matt Olson to load the bases. Frasso got Dubon to fly out to end the threat. Brennan Bernardino threw a scoreless fifth for the Rockies. Perez needed just four pitches to record the first two outs of the sixth. From there, though, Hunter Goodman walked, TJ Rumfield singled and Connor Norby walked to load the bases. Perez allowed the game's first run on Castro's single to left. Suter relieved Perez and got Mickey Moniak to ground out. Perez struck out six and walked two across 5 2/3 frames, allowing one run and five hits. After Harris began the seventh with an infield single, Ozzie Albies fouled an 0-2 pitch off the mask of home plate umpire Ron Kulpa that forced him to exit. After a 13-minute delay, play resumed with Herget plunking Albies. Mike Yastrzemski then grounded into a double play. Jaden Hill relieved Herget and walked Austin Riley, but fanned Lane Thomas to end the threat. --Field Level Media

item.title: Dylan Crews, Nationals walk off Marlins in 10th inning
item.description: Dylan Crews' two-out bases-loaded single in the 10th gave the host Washington Nationals a 5-4 win over the Miami Marlins on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Dylan Crews' two-out bases-loaded single in the 10th gave the host Washington Nationals a 5-4 win over the Miami Marlins on Saturday. It was Crews' first career walk-off hit and the first walk-off win of the season for the Nationals, who won their third straight. Heriberto Hernandez homered for the Marlins, who have lost four of their last five. Crews lined an 0-1 four-seam fastball from Michael Petersen (3-4) into right-center field to end it. Orlando Ribalta (1-2), who pitched the 10th, got the win. Nationals starter Cade Cavalli left the game after taking Javier Sanoja's liner off his right calf with two out in the fourth. He recovered to throw Sanoja out at first to end the half inning but limped to the dugout. Cavalli did not allow a hit in four innings with three walks and eight strikeouts. He is 12-5 with a 3.12 ERA with 177 strikeouts in 152 2/3 innings for the season. Marlins starter Sandy Alcantara gave up four runs and eight hits in six innings with a walk and three strikeouts. Miami tied the game 4-4 with four runs in the seventh, all with two out. Kyle Stowers hit a two-run double and Hernandez launched a two-run homer off Brad Lord, who allowed all four. It was Hernandez's 22nd homer of the season, a 413-foot drive over the left-center-field fence. Washington took a 4-0 lead in the third inning. The first two scored on catcher Joe Mack's throwing error on Crews' infield single down the first-base line that allowed Jose Pena and Daylen Lile to score. Brady House's two-out RBI single made it 3-0, and he came in on Jorbit Vivas' double. After striking out the side in the first, Cavalli walked the bases loaded with one out in the second but then fanned Owen Caissie and Mack to escape the jam. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rays outscore Padres in wild 7th, hold on to win series
item.description: Chandler Simpson slashed a tiebreaking, two-out single to cap a four-run, seventh-inning rally, lifting the Tampa Bay Rays to a wild 7-6 victory and a series win over the San Diego Padres on Saturday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Chandler Simpson slashed a tiebreaking, two-out single to cap a four-run, seventh-inning rally, lifting the Tampa Bay Rays to a wild 7-6 victory and a series win over the San Diego Padres on Saturday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Fla. Down 6-3 after San Diego's three-run top half of the seventh, Yandy Diaz lasered a bases-loaded single off the center field wall. San Diego second baseman Luis Rengifo then threw home, but his right leg buckled as he turned. The toss went wide and to the backstop for an error to tie it at 6. Rengifo then had to be carted off the field with the injury. After that delay, Simpson slashed a two-out single for a 7-6 lead off reliever Adrian Morejon. Tampa Bay's Jonathan Aranda hit a tape-measure home run, and Junior Caminero ripped his 36th to tie Houston's Yordan Alvarez for the American League lead. Liam Hicks and Taylor Walls had two hits. Starting pitcher Nick Martinez allowed three runs on seven hits in six innings with four strikeouts and no walks Reliever Kevin Kelly (6-3) pitched 1 2/3 scoreless innings, while Bryan Baker recorded his 39th save. San Diego's Dustin Harris had three hits, two runs and a stolen base. Ty France had two hits, including a two-run homer. Manny Machado had two hits and two RBIs. Bradgley Rodriguez (3-3) allowed four runs (one earned) on three hits and a walk without retiring a batter. Starter Walker Buehler tossed five-plus innings and yielded three runs on seven hits with three strikeouts. With one out in the third in a 1-1 game, the home side took its second lead when Aranda hit a 453-foot solo shot to center. His 17th homer came off Buehler's change-up and landed in the netting above the blue batter's eye. In the sixth, France put the visitors ahead for the first time by angling Martinez's 93 mph fastball over the 322-foot mark down the right field line, his 100th career home run, for a 3-2 lead. However, Caminero reached down in the zone and lined a 3-2 cutter - with a 17-degree launch angle -- over the center field wall to match Alvarez's total. Fernando Tatis Jr. put down a perfect bunt in the seventh to fill the bases with no outs. With one out, Machado grounded a single to right to score Rengifo and Harris. A double steal by Tatis and Machado put the Padres up 6-3 as they sent nine batters to the plate. --Field Level Media

item.title: Juan Soto returns, as Mets defeat Astros
item.description: Nolan McLean tossed seven innings of two-hit ball and earned the win Saturday for the host New York Mets, who beat the Houston Astros 6-2 in the middle game of a three-game interleague series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nolan McLean tossed seven innings of two-hit ball and earned the win Saturday for the host New York Mets, who beat the Houston Astros 6-2 in the middle game of a three-game interleague series. Juan Soto returned from the injured list after sitting out five weeks due to strained left calf and went 1-for-4 with the tie-breaking RBI single in the fifth for the Mets. Jared Young had three hits and three RBIs, including a two-run triple to close out the fifth-inning rally, as New York improved to 14-11 this month. The three RBIs were a career-high for Young, who previously had nine two-RBI games. Francisco Alvarez provided eighth-inning insurance with a two-RBI double. Brett Baty had two hits, while Marcus Semien added two hits and a stolen base. Yordan Alvarez homered and had a sacrifice fly for the American League West-leading Astros, who fell to 3-2 on their New York road trip. Alvarez also had Houston's only other hit off McLean, a sixth-inning single. That hit snapped a streak of 11 straight batters retired by McLean (10-8), who gave up an unearned run and issued three walks while striking out four. The only runner who advanced past first against McLean was Jeremy Pena, who laced a leadoff double in the first and advanced to third when Baty misplayed the ball in left before trotting home on Alvarez's fly to right. The seven innings tied a season high for McLean, who has lasted at least six innings in 13 of his last 15 starts. Daniel Duarte gave up Alvarez's 436-foot homer to right. Kodai Senga allowed a leadoff double to Jose Altuve in the ninth before retiring the final three batters in a non-save situation. Bulk reliever Cristian Javier (1-5) took the loss for the Astros after giving up three runs on six hits and no walks while striking out four over 4 1/3 innings. Bennett Sousa gave up one run on one hit while walking two in two-thirds of an inning as an opener. It was Sousa's first big league start. --Field Level Media

item.title: Josh Rojas drives in 4 as red-hot Royals rally past Guardians
item.description: Josh Rojas hit a two-run homer and tied his career high with four RBIs as the surging Kansas City Royals scored eight straight runs to beat the host Cleveland Guardians 8-3 on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Josh Rojas hit a two-run homer and tied his career high with four RBIs as the surging Kansas City Royals scored eight straight runs to beat the host Cleveland Guardians 8-3 on Saturday afternoon. Rojas had a two-run single in the sixth inning and added a two-run homer in the eighth to lift Kansas City to its 12th win in 13 games. The Royals pulled within 6 1/2 games of Cleveland for the third American League wild-card spot. Royals reliever Anthony Gose (1-0) retired all five batters he faced to collect his first victory since June 17, 2022, while pitching for the Guardians against the Los Angeles Dodgers. Cleveland reliever Colin Holderman (6-4) recorded only one out and was charged with four runs, three of them earned. Angel Martinez had a two-run homer off starter Daniel Lynch IV for Cleveland, which sits one game ahead of the Baltimore Orioles in the wild-card race. The Guardians have lost two straight games after winning their previous seven. Kansas City clinched the series, marking just the fifth series victory in its past 27 trips to Cleveland. Lynch went 3 1/3 innings in his fifth start, giving up two runs on three hits with two walks and three strikeouts. The Royals trailed 2-0 in the fifth when Isaac Collins hit a two-run double off Guardians starter Foster Griffin, a 2026 National League All-Star with Washington. Griffin gave up two runs on four hits over five innings, striking out four with one walk. Salvador Perez triggered a four-run outburst in the sixth by driving in Bobby Witt Jr. with a double off Holderman. After Jac Caglianone scored on a Jose Ramirez error, Rojas greeted reliever Erik Sabrowski with a single that drove in Nick Loftin and John Rave to push Kansas City's advantage to 6-2. Gose, Craig Kimbrel, John Schreiber and Nate Pearson combined to retire 14 consecutive hitters from the fourth inning through the eighth. Alex Lange surrendered a Martinez RBI single in the ninth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bryce Eldridge leads Giants to split-earning win over D-backs
item.description: Bryce Eldridge matched career highs with four hits and four RBIs, Rafael Devers drove in two runs with a pair of singles, and the San Francisco Giants salvaged a doubleheader split with the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks with a 7-2 victory in the nightcap Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Bryce Eldridge matched career highs with four hits and four RBIs, Rafael Devers drove in two runs with a pair of singles, and the San Francisco Giants salvaged a doubleheader split with the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks with a 7-2 victory in the nightcap Saturday night. Despite the split, which began with a 7-1 win in Saturday's opener, the Diamondbacks were able to move into a virtual tie with the San Diego Padres, who lost at Tampa Bay, for the National League's third wild-card spot. In a duel of rookie pitchers that followed a number-retirement ceremony for Jeff Kent, the Giants and Diamondbacks battled to a 1-1 tie through 4 1/2 innings of Game 2 until San Francisco ended Mitch Bratt's day with a single by Grant McCray, a walk to Osleivis Basabe and a sacrifice bunt by Christian Koss. After pinch hitter Drew Gilbert worked a walk from reliever Gerardo Carrillo to load the bases, Devers gave the Giants the lead for good with an RBI single. Eldridge then singled home a pair of runs for a 4-1 advantage. Bratt (1-3) was charged with three runs on three hits in 4 1/3 innings. He walked two and struck out two. Making his major league debut after a promotion from Double-A Richmond, Giants right-hander Yunior Marte worked 4 2/3 innings, limiting the Diamondbacks to one run and three hits. He walked two and struck out three. Reiver Sanmartin (2-0), who relieved Marte with two outs in the fifth with the game tied at 1-1, was credited with the win after facing just one batter, striking out Game 1 hero Lars Nootbaar to lead into the Giants' uprising. The clubs traded runs in the seventh, after which Giants relievers Carson Seymour and Dylan Smith slammed the door on the Diamondbacks, sending them to just their third defeat in 13 games against San Francisco in the season series. Gilbert, who drew his second consecutive walk, scored the Giants' seventh-inning run. He also walked and scored in a two-run eighth. Devers and Eldridge drove in the eighth-inning runs. Basabe scored twice for the Giants, who completed a 4-3 homestand. Ildemaro Vargas had two hits for the Diamondbacks, who like the Giants will get a rare Sunday off. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hrgovic storms back to defeat Itauma for IBF heavyweight title
item.description: Croatian Filip Hrgovic pulled off a stunning comeback to beat British prodigy Moses Itauma by technical knockout to claim the vacant IBF world heavyweight title in thrilling fashion.
item.dc:creator: Philip O'connor
item.content:encoded: Croatian Filip Hrgovic pulled off a stunning comeback to beat British prodigy Moses Itauma by technical knockout to claim the vacant IBF world heavyweight title in thrilling fashion at London's O2 Arena on Saturday. Outpointed over the first eight rounds, the 34-year-old Croatian turned the tide in the ninth, taking advantage of his young opponent's exhaustion to force the stoppage in the ninth round to become Croatia's first heavyweight world champion. Itauma came into Saturday's bout with 12 knockouts in 14 professional fights unbeaten, and it looked like he was about to add a 13th as he pounded his opponent with powerful punches to the head and body. Attempting to become the second-youngest heavyweight champion of the world behind Mike Tyson, the 21-year-old's fast hands connected repeatedly with Hrgovic's head, but the Croatian displayed tremendous resilience, despite being on the receiving end of a standing eight count early in the fight. Itauma landed a stunning uppercut as the bell sounded to end the fifth round, but Hrgovic managed to recover, and he played with fire again at the end of the sixth as Itauma pounded him late in the frame. Worn out from his efforts, Itauma slowed as the fight wore on and Hrgovic pounced in the ninth, forcing the young Briton back onto the ropes and overwhelming him with shots, forcing the referee to call off the fight as the towel came in from Itauma's corner. "He's an amazing fighter, I want to thank him for accepting this fight, to give me a chance to become a new star in the heavyweight division. I am the present, and he is definitely the future," Hrgovic said. "He's an amazing fighter, he's one of a kind, he's the best I've been in the ring with, but he needs more experience. He gassed out ... I knew that I have that pace in my favour." Hrgovic said he wants a unification fight against WBC champion Agit Kabayel, who stepped into the ring to congratulate the new champion, but promoter Frank Warren quickly killed that idea, saying that he must fight Frank Sanchez next.

item.title: William Jewell RB MicahJo Barnett dies after medical emergency during game
item.description: William Jewell College running back MicahJo Barnett had a medical emergency on the sideline during the school's season opener on Saturday and the school later announced his death.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: William Jewell College running back MicahJo Barnett had a medical emergency on the sideline during the school's season opener on Saturday and the school later announced his death. Barnett, a junior, reportedly experienced seizure-like symptoms during the first quarter of the Division II contest against Fort Lewis College. The game was played on William Jewell's campus in Liberty, Mo., about 20 miles northeast of Kansas City. Barnett experienced the emergency at approximately 12:20 p.m. local time. Paramedics from the Liberty Fire Department took him to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The game was suspended after the medical episode and subsequently canceled. "William Jewell College and the Liberty, Missouri, community mourn the passing of MicahJo Barnett, junior business administration major and member of Jewell Cardinal Football team and former Liberty North Eagle," the school wrote on its website. "Our thoughts and prayers are with MicahJo's family, our students, the Cardinal Football family, and the rest of our community during this time of loss." Officials planned a vigil Saturday night on the school's quad to honor Barnett and his family. "Our hearts are heavy, and we just appreciate all of the support that we have received from the greater community," William Jewell interim president Dr. Drew Van Horn said Saturday afternoon. "I want to say that we appreciate the response that we've received from the sheriff's office, the police department, the EMS department, our school, the physician for the team. Everybody responded so quickly, so well," Van Horn said. The athletic department's X account posted a photo of Barnett with the heading "Forever a Cardinal" and an illustration of a broken heart. Barnett rushed six times for 29 yards during the game, which included a 1-yard touchdown run at the 5:15 mark of the first quarter for the game's lone score. The game was halted with 4:32 left in the first. Barnett, an academic all-conference honoree in 2025, was beginning his third season with the Cardinals. The native of Shawnee Mission, Kan., rushed for 366 yards and four touchdowns in five games last season before sustaining a season-ending injury. In 2024, he rushed for 91 yards and two scores in eight games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Blue Jays rally from 3 down to edge Mariners
item.description: Alejandro Kirk singled in the go-ahead run in a two-run sixth, Jose Soriano pitched seven effective innings and the Toronto Blue Jays defeated the visiting Seattle Mariners 4-3 on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alejandro Kirk singled in the go-ahead run in a two-run sixth, Jose Soriano pitched seven effective innings and the Toronto Blue Jays defeated the visiting Seattle Mariners 4-3 on Saturday afternoon. The Blue Jays won their second in a row to open the three-game series on a day when former Blue Jays catcher, manager and broadcaster Buck Martinez was inducted into the Blue Jays' new Hall of Excellence. Soriano (11-7) allowed three runs, five hits and two walks while striking out six. Louis Varland pitched the ninth to earn his 31st save. Cal Raleigh hit a solo home run for the Mariners. Seattle took a 1-0 lead in the second when Raleigh lined an elevated 0-1 fastball to right for his 19th homer of the season. The Mariners added two in the fourth. Josh Naylor singled over the bag at first base with two out and Raleigh and Cole Young walked to load the bases. Taylor Ward lined a first-pitch single to left that scored two runs. Toronto cut the lead to 3-2 in the fifth. Myles Straw hit an infield single to second with one out and Brett Bateman walked. Eduard Bazardo replaced starter Kade Anderson, who was making his second career major league start, and struck out Kirk before walking Vladimir Guerrero Jr. to load the bases. George Springer drew a bases-loaded walk on a wild pitch to force in a run, and Bateman also scored as the ball got away. Anderson allowed two runs, three hits and three walks with three strikeouts in 4 1/3 innings. Toronto took a 4-3 lead in the sixth against Jose Ferrer (4-3). Charles McAdoo and Straw walked. Bateman grounded an RBI single with two out that found a hole through the left side of the infield. Kirk's single to right scored the go-ahead run and Carlos Vargas replaced Ferrer. Vargas retired all seven batters he faced. Tyler Rogers allowed a two-out walk to Julio Rodriguez in the eighth. Mason Fluharty replaced Rogers and allowed Naylor's single to right to put runners at the corners before striking out Raleigh. --Field Level Media

item.title: Djokovic says early exit in Cincinnati helped him prepare for US Open
item.description: He said he had a couple weeks to train and get his body and mind "into the right state" heading into New York.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Novak Djokovic said he is never satisfied with early losses but that his second-round exit at the Cincinnati Open gave him extra time to prepare for the U.S. Open, where he will chase a record 25th Grand Slam singles crown. The world number five fell to Argentine Thiago Agustin Tirante in Cincinnati after struggling in the heat and requiring a medical timeout. "I don't like early losses anywhere, to be honest, but it gave me time to be preparing for the U.S. Open in a most adequate way," the 39-year-old Serbian told reporters in Flushing Meadows on Saturday. He said he had a couple weeks to train and get his body and mind "into the right state" heading into New York. "If you ask me if I'm prepared, I feel like I am, as best as I can be, but it's different training and then getting out on the Arthur Ashe Stadium and playing best-of-five (sets)," Djokovic said. "The opening matches are always for me, particularly in the last few years, quite challenging," he added. "So hopefully I can overcome the first hurdle and build from there." Djokovic also said he was proud to be appearing at his 20th U.S. Open, which he has won four times. "Obviously longevity was always one of the goals when I was younger, trying to have long career, trying to have more shots at Grand Slams, and stay healthy long enough so that I can perform for as many years as possible," he said. Fourth seed Djokovic will open campaign against Argentine Mariano Navone.

item.title: Rybakina on track to recover from injury and play at US Open
item.description: World number two Elena Rybakina said she is on track to play at the U.S. Open as she recovers from a leg injury suffered at the Cincinnati Open earlier this month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: World number two Elena Rybakina said she is on track to play at the U.S. Open as she recovers from a leg injury suffered at the Cincinnati Open earlier this month. The twice Grand Slam winner retired in the first set of her Cincinnati quarter-final match against Iga Swiatek on August 20 with an ankle problem. "I'm quite confident with the decision we are making each day how to practice, what to do, and especially what can happen worst-case scenario. So all these things I feel quite confident," Rybakina told reporters at Flushing Meadows on Saturday. "I just feel like it's just few more days and I should be very fine." Kazakhstan's Rybakina, 27, said it was painful to walk for a couple of days after suffering the injury, but she is glad with how her recovery process is going. "We will see what's gonna happen in the next few days, but for now it's been well," she said. "I always want to go on court when I'm 100% sure, and it's the last slam of the year, so I think everyone will want to try to compete." Rybakina is set to open her U.S. Open campaign against American Thea Frodin.

item.title: Reports: Dolphins trade QB Quinn Ewers to Jaguars
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars are acquiring second-year quarterback Quinn Ewers from the Miami Dolphins, according to multiple reports.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Jacksonville Jaguars are acquiring second-year quarterback Quinn Ewers from the Miami Dolphins, according to multiple reports. The Jaguars are sending the Dolphins their sixth-round pick in 2028, per ESPN. Ewers was the Dolphins' seventh-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. The Texas product went on to appear in four games for the Dolphins last season, including three starts, as he threw for 622 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions that netted an 85.5 passer rating. The 23-year-old adds depth behind starter Trevor Lawrence in Jacksonville. Veteran Nick Mullens, 31, owns a 5-15 record as a starter while Carter Bradley and Joey Aguilar have not taken a regular-season NFL snap. The Dolphins have three quarterbacks left on their depth chart: offseason acquisition Malik Willis, Cam Miller and Mark Gronowski. --Field Level Media

item.title: Wawrinka relishing final US Open in farewell season
item.description: Three-time Grand Slam winner Stan Wawrinka is soaking in the opportunity to play at the U.S. Open one last time, with the Swiss set to retire at the end of the season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Three-time Grand Slam winner Stan Wawrinka is soaking in the opportunity to play at the U.S. Open one last time, with the Swiss set to retire at the end of the season. The 2016 U.S. Open champion, now ranked 127th, had initially been overlooked for a wildcard into the men's singles draw but was belatedly granted one after several days of outcry from fans over his exclusion. When American wildcard Patrick Kypson pulled out injured, Wawrinka received a call late on Wednesday confirming that he had been given a place in the draw. "It's my last Grand Slam of my career, so of course it's going to be special when I'm gonna play the match. That's for sure," the 41-year-old Swiss told reporters in Flushing Meadows on Saturday. "I'm going to feel it. That's a no-brainer. But I'm super excited. I'm happy. I'm enjoying the fact that I have this opportunity to be here one last time." The former world number three participated in the Australian Open, French Open and Wimbledon this year on wildcards. Wawrinka said when he was aspiring to be a top player, he told himself he would only think about regrets after his career came to a close. "I think I did everything possible to be the best version of a tennis player I could. I always push myself all those years, trying to give everything on the court and off the court. So with that, I'm quite in peace with myself," he said. "I know I couldn't do it more. I know I took all the opportunity I had. Of course, I have some small regret. Of course, there is many match I would love to change the score, but at the end, like I say, I think I'm in peace with myself."

item.title: Australia defeat Argentina to maintain unbeaten start for coach Kiss
item.description: Tom Hooper scored a crucial second half try in a superb all-round display as Australia defeated a young Argentina side 27-21 in the opening match of their two-test tour in San Salvador de Jujuy on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tom Hooper scored a crucial second half try in a superb all-round display as Australia defeated a young Argentina side 27-21 in the opening match of their two-test tour in San Salvador de Jujuy on Saturday. Australia won the forward battle with the dynamic Hooper and back row teammates Fraser McReight and number eight Rob Valetini giving the visitors the ascendancy as new coach Les Kiss was able to celebrate a third successive win since taking over. It was his most impressive against a largely inexperienced but energetic Argentina who had run world champions South Africa close earlier in the month and thrive on chaos. Australia scored four tries through hooker Brandon Paenga-Amosa, flyhalf Carter Gordon, McReight and Hooper and took their chances, mixed with some scrambling defence. "It was a back and forth sort of match," McReight said. "Argentina were really good and we were poor in some areas, just really proud of the group and happy we got the win over here. "I am really happy with the way the group was able to rebound from a mistake, come back quickly and gather ourselves. We are building." Argentina might rue some soft moments on defence but scored three tries themselves as fullback Geronimo Prisciantelli, number eight Joaquin Moro and prop Boris Wenger all crossed. There were enough positives for the home side to move on to the second test in imposing Mendoza next Saturday with some confidence, though they will want to be much better in possession. By contrast, some slick handling from the Australia forwards ended with Paenga-Amosa scoring the opening try, before Gordon added a second score. Prisciantelli crossed for Argentina’s first try following fine work from wing Rodrigo Isgro, but McReight added a third for the visitors soon afterwards. Following a yellow card for wing Harry Potter after a deliberate knockdown, Australia had to weather heavy pressure and Moro crossed as the visitors led 22-14 at halftime. Wenger added another score to reduce the deficit to one point, but the momentum swung again when almost immediately Hooper scored Australia’s fourth try. The visitors missed the chance to kill the contest as replacement Tate McDermott was held up over the line when he seemed certain to score. But poor handling in the closing minutes again denied Argentina the chance to launch a final assault on the Australian line and the visitors held on for victory.

item.title: Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong blasts 3 homers, drives in 6 to thrash Reds
item.description: Pete Crow-Armstrong recorded his first three-homer game and drove in six runs to power the host Chicago Cubs to a 17-5 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Pete Crow-Armstrong recorded his first three-homer game and drove in six runs to power the host Chicago Cubs to a 17-5 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Saturday. Crow-Armstrong increased his team-leading homer total to 36 with a solo shot in the first inning, a two-run blast in the second and a three-run homer in the seventh. Chicago's Carson Kelly launched a three-run homer and had an RBI double. Seiya Suzuki belted a two-run homer while Alex Bregman also went deep and added an RBI single to highlight their three-hit performances. Tyrone Taylor matched Crow-Armstrong with four of the Cubs' 19 hits and Nico Hoerner added an RBI single to help the team snap a three-game losing skid. The power display backed Kevin Gausman (8-11), who allowed five runs on six hits in five innings. Cincinnati rookie Sal Stewart belted a two-run shot for his team-leading 30th homer of the season. Eugenio Suarez also had a two-run homer and JJ Bleday added a sacrifice fly for the Reds, who lost for the 10th time in 15 games. Crow-Armstrong opened the scoring by depositing a 0-1 fastball from Andrew Abbott (6-10) over the wall in right-center to lead off the first. Suzuki followed with a single, and Bregman sent a 0-2 curveball over the wall in center to stake Chicago to a 3-0 lead. Suarez trimmed his team's deficit to 3-2 by jumping on a Gausman fastball in the second. Taylor extended the Cubs' lead to 4-2 by scoring on a throwing error in the second before Crow-Armstrong blasted a 1-2 curveball from Abbott over the wall in right. Stewart answered with a two-run homer in the third inning. However, Bregman gave the Cubs a 7-4 lead in the fourth when he recorded his team's third straight single to score Crow-Armstrong. Bleday's sacrifice fly brought the Reds within two in the top of the fifth, but Kelly and Crow-Armstrong effectively put the game out of reach with their respective three-run homers. Abbott lost his third consecutive start after permitting seven runs on eight hits in three innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Andrew Benintendi carries White Sox past Twins
item.description: Andrew Benintendi went 3-for-4 with a double, a homer and two RBIs, and the Chicago White Sox held on for a 3-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Saturday afternoon in Minneapolis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Andrew Benintendi went 3-for-4 with a double, a homer and two RBIs, and the Chicago White Sox held on for a 3-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Saturday afternoon in Minneapolis. Benintendi's three hits marked the only hits of the day for Chicago, which won anyway to extend its winning streak to four games. The White Sox will look to complete a three-game sweep on Sunday afternoon. Josh Bell and Walker Jenkins each went 1-for-3 with an RBI for Minnesota. Luke Keaschall added a double. White Sox right-hander Erick Fedde (7-8) earned the victory. He held the Twins to two runs on three hits in five innings, and he walked two and struck out four. Twins right-hander Andrew Morris (4-7) allowed one run on one hit in two innings of relief. He followed starter Bailey Ober, who allowed two runs (one earned) on two hits in five innings. White Sox left-hander Bryan Hudson pitched a scoreless ninth for his seventh save of the season and his second save in as many games. The White Sox opened the scoring in the top of the first, when Benintendi singled to shallow right field to drive in Sam Antonacci. The Twins responded in the bottom of the first to even the score at 1. Bell hit a sacrifice fly to deep right field to drive in Keaschall. In the bottom of the second, Jenkins notched his first career RBI to put the Twins on top 2-1. He hit into a groundout that allowed Kaelen Culpepper to score. Jenkins made his big-league debut on Friday, when he recorded his first career hit against the White Sox. A fielding error by Culpepper opened the door for the White Sox to pull even at 2 in the fourth. Benintendi scored from third on the play. Benintendi delivered the go-ahead homer in the top of the sixth. The blast to right field marked his 14th homer of the season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Joshua Dobbs guides Lions over Colts in preseason finale
item.description: Joshua Dobbs had an efficient outing, guiding the Detroit Lions to a 25-16 road victory over the Indianapolis Colts in their preseason finale.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joshua Dobbs had an efficient outing, guiding the Detroit Lions to a 25-16 road victory over the Indianapolis Colts in their preseason finale. Dobbs completed 15 of 19 pass attempts for 128 yards and two touchdowns. Jacob Saylors also shined with 17 carries for 100 yards on the ground. On the opening drive, the Colts' Anthony Richardson Sr. connected with Keenan Allen for a 24-yard completion, which set up a 46-yard Blake Grupe field goal. Lions starter Luke Altmyer was intercepted by Sauce Gardner on the following drive. The undrafted rookie quarterback completed seven of 11 pass attempts for 55 yards and the lone pick. Altmyer led the Lions on a 75-yard drive late in the first quarter, culminating in a 1-yard Trayveon Williams touchdown run. The Lions pulled away in the second quarter behind two touchdown passes from Dobbs. He hit Jackson Meeks for a 6-yard score, then connected with Tay Martin for a 2-yard touchdown to lift the Lions ahead 19-13. The Colts scored their only touchdown of the game in the second quarter on a DJ Giddens 6-yard rushing score. Richardson led the Colts with 80 passing yards. As a team, Indianapolis only posted 34 rushing yards. Seth McGowan was the leading rusher for the Colts with four carries for 20 yards. Notably, the Lions overcame four turnovers in the victory. They went an efficient 4-for-4 in their red zone opportunities. --Field Level Media

item.title: Defense, starting pitching help Red Sox blank Yankees
item.description: Rookie Jake Bennett pitched six stellar innings and got some massive help from his defense in the fourth inning as the visiting Boston Red Sox earned a 6-0 victory over the New York Yankees in the opener of Saturday's day-night doubleheader.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rookie Jake Bennett pitched six stellar innings and got some massive help from his defense in the fourth inning as the visiting Boston Red Sox earned a 6-0 victory over the New York Yankees in the opener of Saturday's day-night doubleheader. Wilyer Abreu homered in the first inning against New York starter Carlos Rodon (4-3) as the Red Sox took a 6-5 lead in the season series and moved back to within two games of the Yankees for the AL's top wild-card spot and home-field advantage in a wild-card series. Bennett (9-6) allowed three hits in his fourth career scoreless start. He struck out seven without a walk and has allowed one run on six hits in 12 1/3 innings during his two starts against New York. New York's biggest threat against the left-hander occurred with one out in the fourth when Amed Rosario reached on a throwing error by third baseman Caleb Durbin and advanced on a passed ball by catcher Adley Rutschman. Heliot Ramos doubled when center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela got turned around and third base coach Luis Rojas waved Rosario home. Rafaela recovered at the warning track and threw to second baseman Nick Sogard, who nailed Rosario at the plate with a good throw to Rutschman. Rutschman recorded the second out by tagging Rosario on the leg and Bennett finished the fourth with a called third strike on Cody Bellinger. Boston added its second run in the fifth when Rutschman singled and advanced on a throwing error by Rosario at second base on a lineout. Following a single by Sogard, he scored on a passed ball by catcher Ali Sanchez. Rutschman completed his first three-hit game with Boston when he singled and scored alongside Durbin on Andruw Monasterio's two-run single. Sogard followed with an RBI double to score Monasterio, and Rafaela added an RBI single to cap the inning. Rodon allowed two runs on three hits in 4 2/3 innings during his third start back from left elbow inflammation. The left-hander struck out five and walked one. After Bennett's 83-pitch outing, Tyron Guerrero and Garrett Whitlock pitched an inning apiece before the Red Sox padded the lead. Jovani Moran closed out the game with a perfect ninth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kevin McGonigle, Javier Baez help Tigers tame Dodgers
item.description: Kevin McGonigle delivered a bases-loaded single in the ninth to drive in the winning run as the host Detroit Tigers topped the Los Angeles Dodgers 2-1 on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kevin McGonigle delivered a bases-loaded single in the ninth to drive in the winning run as the host Detroit Tigers topped the Los Angeles Dodgers 2-1 on Saturday afternoon. Javier Baez scored both runs for Detroit, which had lost eight of its previous nine games. Gleyber Torres drove in the other run for Detroit. Kenley Jansen (4-5) picked up the win in relief. Starter Keider Montero gave up one run and four hits in 5 1/3 innings. Andrew Sears tossed 2 2/3 innings of scoreless relief. Freddie Freeman drove in the lone run as the Dodgers lost for the fourth time in five games. Los Angeles has dropped 10 one-run games since the All-Star break. Starter Blake Snell gave up one run and three hits in five innings while striking out 10. With two out and a runner on second in the top of the ninth, Teoscar Hernandez hit a deep fly ball that left fielder Baez tracked down to keep the score tied. Baez then led off the ninth against Jack Dreyer (5-2) with a double down the left field line. Max Clark's sacrifice bunt moved Baez to third. Torres was given an intentional walk and Hao-Yu Lee drew a walk to load the bases. McGonigle then ripped a 1-2 pitch into the left-center field gap to end the game. The Tigers scored in the third but came away lamenting they didn't get more runs. Baez drew a leadoff walk and Clark reached on an error after laying down a bunt. Torres ripped a ground-rule double to the opposite field that knocked in Baez. Snell briefly left the field after Lee popped out. After walking McGonigle, Snell then proceeded to strike out Dillon Dingler and Eduardo Valencia to leave the runners stranded. Los Angeles broke through in the sixth. Alek Thomas led off with an opposite-field double and moved to third on a groundout. Freeman then ripped a single to bring in Thomas. The Dodgers eventually loaded the bases with one out but Tyler Holton induced Tommy Edman to bounce into a double play. --Field Level Media
